principles: New project surfaces should use the product name Lattice by default.
Legacy Koala paths must remain accepted and diagnosable for existing repositories.
Brand/name migration must not imply runtime, receipt, or production authority changes.
Smoke coverage must prove both new primary paths and legacy aliases.
drivers: User-visible init output is the first product impression for new projects.
Existing projects may have committed Koala-named wrappers and scripts.
Codex adapter gate evidence consumes manifest/wrapper material paths and must stay fresh.

options.name: Generate both Lattice and Koala files
pros: Maximum immediate command compatibility for fresh projects
Very low risk for users who type old local commands
cons: Fresh projects still show Koala-named files, contradicting the user goal of Lattice naming
Adds duplicate managed assets and more local clutter

options.name: Lattice primary with Koala compatibility recognition
pros: Fresh projects see only Lattice-named local launchers/manifests
Old projects remain supported through detection/check/verify fallback
Matches the existing thin-assets direction of fewer local files
cons: New projects that manually type old bin/koala.js path will need to use the global koala alias or bin/lattice.js

options.name: Hard rename everything and drop Koala aliases
pros: Cleanest brand surface in code and docs
cons: Too large for an init asset migration story

chosen: Lattice primary with Koala compatibility recognition
rationale: This satisfies the user-visible Lattice naming goal for new projects while excluding a destructive hard rename. It keeps old Koala files as compatibility aliases in checks and verification rather than generating duplicate files in new init output.

preMortem.trigger: checkManifest only looks for .Codex/lattice.json after migration
preMortem.consequence: Old repositories cannot pass REVIEW/DONE gate after upgrading core
preMortem.mitigation: Codex verification must resolve primary Lattice manifest first, then legacy Koala manifest fallback with tests for both.

preMortem.scenario: New init still leaves Koala files
preMortem.trigger: Legacy alias wrappers are generated by default for convenience
preMortem.consequence: User sees the exact Koala files they asked to remove
preMortem.mitigation: Fresh init smoke asserts KOALA.md, .Codex/koala.json, bin/koala.js, and bin/koala-codex.js are absent.

preMortem.scenario: Managed check deletes a user-owned legacy wrapper
preMortem.trigger: Profile cleanup treats any Koala path as generated
preMortem.mitigation: Cleanup must only remove files that match generated content; smoke seeds user-owned legacy files and asserts preservation.
